# 0 · Context & ethics (10 min) — instructor script

Run all five beats; the two non-negotiables are **Measurement** (these records
count *reports and enforcement*, not crime itself) and **Consequences** (a
chart of this data can move policy, prices, and policing; the title must say
"reported"). Model sentence for the student prompt: *"Because unreported
offenses never enter the data, every count is a floor, not a level — and the
floor is lower in communities that distrust reporting."*

# 1 · The central question

> **[COMMITTED QUESTION — recommended shape: "How do reported [offense
> category] incidents vary by hour of day?" It exercises the timestamp, gives
> geom_point a natural x-axis, and regenerates every semester with new data.]**

# 2 · E — Extraction (12 min)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)

# LM1: load — note for students: load() puts objects INTO the environment;
# there is no assignment arrow, which is exactly why we inspect ls() next.
load("Data/[FILENAME].RData")
ls()
```
:::


**Expected:** `[OBJECT_NAME]` appears. Contrast with `read_csv()` on the
board: *read functions return, load() injects.* This is the whole CLO 2.7
lesson in one line.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# LM2: inspect
glimpse([OBJECT_NAME])
```
:::


**Expected:** [rows], [date range], one row = one reported incident.

# 3 · T — Transformation (28 min)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# LM3: select
crime_small_df <- [OBJECT_NAME] |>
  select(offense, date_time, [neighborhood_or_beat])
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# LM4: filter — committed rule: [e.g., offense %in% c(...), complete
# date_time, incidents within the chosen year]
crime_clean_df <- crime_small_df |>
  filter([RULE])

nrow(crime_small_df) - nrow(crime_clean_df)
```
:::


**Expected:** [n removed]. Defense: [state it — and connect to underreporting:
we can defend removing *unusable records*; we cannot recover *unreported
incidents*, and the answer must say so].


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# LM5: recode/create — recommended: hour of day
crime_clean_df <- crime_clean_df |>
  mutate(hour = lubridate::hour(date_time))
```
:::


*(If lubridate hasn't formally arrived yet, this is a one-function toolbox
loan — name it, use it, move on.)*


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# LM6: group + summarize + arrange
crime_summary_df <- crime_clean_df |>
  group_by(hour) |>
  summarize(n = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(n))

crime_summary_df
```
:::


**Expected:** [peak hours — typically late evening for most offense mixes].

# 4 · V — Visualization & summary (20 min)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# LM8: the point plot
ggplot(crime_summary_df, aes(x = hour, y = n)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#12263A") +
  labs(
    x = "Hour of day",
    y = "Number of reported incidents",
    title = "Reported [offense] incidents peak in the [period]",
    subtitle = "Reports, not occurrences — see limitations"
  )
```
:::


**Expected pattern:** [describe once committed]. The subtitle is mandatory —
it is the Transparency beat (12.6) enforced in the artifact itself.

# 5 · Interpretation & final answer (10 min) — model answer shape

> *"Reported [offense] incidents are concentrated in [period], with roughly
> [X]× as many reports at the peak hour as at the quietest hour. This pattern
> describes when incidents are REPORTED, which reflects both when events occur
> and when people or patrols are positioned to report them — enforcement and
> reporting behavior are baked into every count. [One consequence sentence:
> what this chart should and should not be used to decide.]"*

Trio check (CLO 4.5): pattern ✔ · magnitude ✔ · caveat ✔ — same rubric as
Cycles 01 and 02, now carrying the heaviest ethical weight of the three.
